Pre-cursor sensor level activities haveidentified AlO (aluminium oxide band and associate lithium markers) and SWIR (shortwave infrared) as the most promising and accessible wavelengths from orbit that most re-entry events of artificial will have in common. The study shall establish the system level accommodation of such a sensor suite on a large CubeSat or small satellite platform with capable AOCS suite for pointing and orbit control.As uncontrolled or controlled re-entry events can occur anywhere on the globe, it is envisaged the satelliteplatform shall be in a relatively high orbit to ensure the field of view of the sensors can point to the re-entry streaks generated(which can last for 100'sof km) and preferential observation geometries (such as re-entry event in the Earth shadow) can be reached on average for 1 out of the on average 3 re-entries daily within the forecasting period of a ground segment (roughly two days prior to the event). The mobility needs of the platform shall thus be an integral part of the phase A level tradeoffs.To prepare for the above-described mission, the proposed activity will assess the overall feasibility of the mission and specifically include: Mission and requirements definition: redefine in detail the purpose and mission objectives deriving consistently the satellite system, theorbital, and the groundsegment requirements. These shall be derived from the identified need on regularly observing re-entry events. Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the satellite will be developed.
